chapter: San Francisco, the So Different Orchestra and Johnny
title: Baron Long's business career and his greeter Paul Jones
summary: Baron Long, who took over Levy's Tavern, later owned the Grant Hotel and the Biltmore and stayed in the background while Paul Jones greeted guests.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Which you said was at the beach. Right?
Which was at Venice, I think it was.
And you said he also owned the Biltmore Hotel?
Later on. After he sold the nightclub in Watts,

he went to San Diego and bought the Grant Hotel. Then from the Grant Hotel, he sold that, I think--I don't know what his business is--but anyway, he bought the Biltmore, and I think he died there a few years ago in the Biltmore. But he was a...uh...man in the background. He had a manager named Paul Jones, I think, was the guy that stood out in front and met everybody and congratulated it, but I don't know what you'd call him but a greeter, but he was so popular that he brought all the people there, you know. He was a popular guy but Baron Long--you'd see him sitting over in the corner, he and his wife having a drink and then he'd go on home. He never did stick around much or anything. He wasn't that kind of a man, but he had the business end of it, so he ran all these places and...but Paul Jones was always the guy that was out in front--the meeter, the greeter, the meeter, whatever you'd call it.
